correctness.rationale: Every nonempty code has uniform opposite endpoints. For the fixed orientation the four three-bit prefix neighborhoods of compatible suffixes form a nested chain, so every code is contained in one of four valid universal Cartesian templates; disjoint boundaries for n at least 6 permit an arbitrary middle. Exact boundary generating polynomials yield the four binomial coefficients and bit complementation supplies the other orientation. Direct binomial asymptotics and polynomial sign comparisons prove the three claimed crossover densities. The verifier independently enumerated 255 prefix subsets, checked 475 weight/length pairs and 24 literal optimum cliques. Finite checks are supplementary.

value.rationale: Natural constant-Hamming-weight optimization of an existing synchronization constraint, not resolved by an unrestricted-cardinality maximum: at extreme densities the unweighted-optimal six-pair templates lose to four-pair templates. Exact maxima for every length n at least 6 and weight, four explicit attaining constructions and the density-dependent golden-ratio changeovers describe a nontrivial design trade-off relevant to sparse and dense marker codes.
